newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria sees $8.0 bln foreign reserves at end-1997.
newsitem.headline: Algeria sees $8.0 bln foreign reserves at end-1997.

text.p: Algeria expects its foreign reserves to reach $8.0 billion at the end of 1997, a rise of $1.6 billion from their level this month, the country's Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia said on Wednesday.
"They (the foreign reserves) will reach $8.0 billion at the ending of this year, God willing," Ouyahia told parliament in a speech broadcast live on Algerian state-run television.
Algeria's foreign reserves were at $6.4 billion at the beginning of August, swelling by $1.0 billion from March, according to official data.
They stood at $4.2 billion in December 1996 compared to $2.11 billion in the same month in 1995, official figures showed.

Officials said the rise in reserves was mainly due to soaring crude oil prices and pruning in the value and volume of Algeria's imports because of a buoyant dollar and de-stocking of imported goods by local companies.

The Algerian government said this week that its oil and gas exports had increased in the first five months this year, thanks to a 7.9 percent rise in volume and 13.1 percent jump in value of hydrocarbon sales abroad.
The government also said it forecast exports of oil and gas would yield $12.5 billion in 1997, up by $1.0 billion from its initial forecasts.
The government set a conservative budgeted target price for Algeria's oil of $17.50 a barrel for the whole year 1997.
The value of Algeria's exports of oil and gas, amounting to more than 90 percent of its total exports, rose to $12.6 billion in 1996, up 29 percent from 1995.
The authorities had said that Algeria's average crude price stood at $21.6 per barrel in 1996 compared to a budgeted average of $16-$17 per barrel in that year.
